#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling

  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"

      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

Cache it per resolved version with `setup/cache.sh dart` (`DART_CACHE_*`).
Network-free inspection: `dart.sh plan` (resolved target/URL/layout) and
`dart.sh status`. Unit-tested in `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`.

Dart-repo runners wire it via `customParams.setupCommands`:
`["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]` (see `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` §3.3).

+# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
+# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
+# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
+# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
+# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
+# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
+# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
+# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
+installed_version() {
+  local d=""
+  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
+    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
+  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    d="$(command -v dart)"
+  fi
+  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
+  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
+    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
+}"}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

Cache it per resolved version with `setup/cache.sh dart` (`DART_CACHE_*`).
Network-free inspection: `dart.sh plan` (resolved target/URL/layout) and
`dart.sh status`. Unit-tested in `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`.

Dart-repo runners wire it via `customParams.setupCommands`:
`["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]` (see `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` §3.3).

{"patch":"[setup/dart.sh#0B1B]
SWAP 56.=70:
+# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
+# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
+# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
+# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
+# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
+# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
+# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
+# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
+installed_version() {
+  local d=""
+  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
+    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
+  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    d="$(command -v dart)"
+  fi
+  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
+  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
+    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
+}"}

87:quality_detection() {
88:  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
89:  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
90:    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
91:    while IFS= read -r kv; do
92:      case "${kv}" in
93:        step=*)    found=1 ;;
94:        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
95:        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
96:      esac
97:    done <<EOF
98:$(awk -v sq="'" '
99:  /uses:[[:space:]]*dart-lang\/setup-dart/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
100:  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
101:  inb && /sdk:/ {
102:    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
103:    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
104:  }
105:  inb && /channel:/ {
106:    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
107:    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
108:  }
109:' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
110:EOF
111:  done
112:  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
113:}

115:# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
116:# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
117:#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
118:#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
119:#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
120:#   4. stable                      → source=default
121:# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
122:# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
123:resolve_target() {
124:  local arg="${1:-}"
125:  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
126:  SOURCE="default"
127:  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
128:    SOURCE="argument"
129:  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
130:    SOURCE="environment"
131:  fi
132:
133:  local det found det_sdk det_channel
134:  det="$(quality_detection)"
135:  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
136:  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
137:
138:  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
139:    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
140:    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
141:    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
142:    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
143:  fi
144:
145:  case "${TARGET}" in
146:    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
147:      MODE="channel"
148:      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
149:      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
150:      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi
151:      [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] && CHANNEL="stable"
152:      case "${CHANNEL}" in stable|beta|dev) ;; *) CHANNEL="stable" ;; esac
153:      VERSION=""
154:      ;;
155:    *)
156:      MODE="version"
157:      VERSION="${TARGET}"
158:      CHANNEL="${det_channel}"
159:      [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] && CHANNEL="stable"
160:      case "${CHANNEL}" in stable|beta|dev) ;; *) CHANNEL="stable" ;; esac
161:      ;;
162:  esac
163:}

165:# dart-archive release URL. Channel mode resolves to `latest` until the
166:# concrete version is fetched at install time.
167:sdk_url() {
168:  local ver="${1:-${VERSION:-latest}}"
169:  [ -n "${ver}" ] || ver="latest"
170:  echo "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/${CHANNEL}/release/${ver}/sdk/dartsdk-${OS}-${ARCH}-release.zip"
171:}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

Cache it per resolved version with `setup/cache.sh dart` (`DART_CACHE_*`).
Network-free inspection: `dart.sh plan` (resolved target/URL/layout) and
`dart.sh status`. Unit-tested in `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`.

Dart-repo runners wire it via `customParams.setupCommands`:
`["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]` (see `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` §3.3).

+# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
+# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
+# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
+# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
+# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
+# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
+# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
+# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
+installed_version() {
+  local d=""
+  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
+    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
+  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    d="$(command -v dart)"
+  fi
+  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
+  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
+    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
+}"}

{"newText":"_cache_dart() {
  # Dart SDK (gh-918: factory legs on dart repos need the same gate toolchain
  # as CI — setup/dart.sh resolves the channel/version and installs under
  # ~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk). Key on the target dart.sh ACTUALLY resolves — the
  # same precedence (explicit dart:<version> arg > DART_VERSION env >
  # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart detection > stable) — so the key the
  # restore step computes ("cache.sh keys dart", BEFORE the install) is the
  # key the save step derives after it, and the primary key can round-trip.
  # (Keying on ${DART_VERSION:-stable} alone keyed the env var, not the
  # resolution: on a beta-pinned repo the restore step exported dart-stable-…
  # while dart.sh installed beta.) dart.sh keeps DART_VERSION a pure input
  # pin — it does not re-export the installed version under it — so this plan
  # call resolves identically before and after the install.
  local version="${1:-}"
  if [ -z "${version}" ]; then
    version="$(bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/dart.sh" plan 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^requested=//p' | head -1)"

  export_var "DART_CACHE_KEY"  "dart-${version}-${OS_TAG}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

SWAP 56.=70:
+# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
+# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
+# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
+# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
+# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
+# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
+# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
+# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
+installed_version() {
+  local d=""
+  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
+    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
+  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    d="$(command -v dart)"
+  fi
+  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
+  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
+    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
+}"}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

Cache it per resolved version with `setup/cache.sh dart` (`DART_CACHE_*`).
Network-free inspection: `dart.sh plan` (resolved target/URL/layout) and
`dart.sh status`. Unit-tested in `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`.

Dart-repo runners wire it via `customParams.setupCommands`:
`["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]` (see `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` §3.3).

{"patch":"[setup/dart.sh#0B1B]
SWAP 56.=70:
+# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
+# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
+# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
+# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
+# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
+# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
+# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
+# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
+installed_version() {
+  local d=""
+  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
+    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
+  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    d="$(command -v dart)"
+  fi
+  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
+  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
+    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
+}"}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;

$(awk -v sq="'" '

  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0

    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }

' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done

  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable

# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

Cache it per resolved version with `setup/cache.sh dart` (`DART_CACHE_*`).
Network-free inspection: `dart.sh plan` (resolved target/URL/layout) and
`dart.sh status`. Unit-tested in `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`.

Dart-repo runners wire it via `customParams.setupCommands`:
`["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]` (see `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` §3.3).

{"patch":"[setup/dart.sh#0B1B]
SWAP 56.=70:
+# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
+# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
+# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
+# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
+# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
+# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
+# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
+# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
+installed_version() {
+  local d=""
+  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
+    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
+  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    d="$(command -v dart)"
+  fi
+  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
+  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
+    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
+}"}

Wait — awk comments inside the awk program: `#` starts a comment in awk ONLY at positions where a statement could end... Actually in awk, `#` begins a comment anywhere a new token can start — inside the program string passed to awk, `  # Comment lines...` on its own line is a valid awk comment. BUT the first comment line is INSIDE the awk single-quoted program:
```
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — ...
```
Yes, awk supports `#` comments in the program text. That's fine.

BUT careful: the single-quoted awk program contains an apostrophe? "commented-out step" — no apostrophe. Let me double check my comment text: "neither a commented-out step ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note." — no single quotes ✓. Second comment: "optionally with a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common in generated/templated workflows)." — no single quotes ✓.

Hmm wait — there's a subtle issue: the `uses` match rule is now UNGUARDED (no `inb &&`), and it comes AFTER the comment-skip rule which is `inb &&` guarded. So a commented `# - uses: dart-lang/...` line BEFORE any step: comment-skip rule doesn't fire (inb=0), second rule doesn't match (# anchor) ✓.

But what about a commented step INSIDE a live block (inb=1)? E.g.:
```
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
      # - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1   (old, disabled)
        channel: beta
```
inb=1; line `# - uses:` → comment-skip fires, next ✓ good.

Also the quoted variant anchored: `- uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1"` — pattern `[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)` ✓.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

115:# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
116:# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
117:#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
118:#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
119:#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
120:#   4. stable                      → source=default
121:# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
122:# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
123:resolve_target() {
124:  local arg="${1:-}"
125:  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
126:  SOURCE="default"
127:  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
128:    SOURCE="argument"
129:  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
130:    SOURCE="environment"
131:  fi
132:
133:  local det found det_sdk det_channel
134:  det="$(quality_detection)"
135:  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
136:  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"
137:
138:  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
139:    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
140:    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
141:    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
142:    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
143:  fi
144:
145:  case "${TARGET}" in
146:    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
147:      MODE="channel"
148:      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
149:      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
150:      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi
151:      [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] && CHANNEL="stable"
152:      case "${CHANNEL}" in stable|beta|dev) ;; *) CHANNEL="stable" ;; esac
153:      VERSION=""
154:      ;;
155:    *)
156:      MODE="version"
157:      VERSION="${TARGET}"
158:      CHANNEL="${det_channel}"
159:      [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] && CHANNEL="stable"
160:      case "${CHANNEL}" in stable|beta|dev) ;; *) CHANNEL="stable" ;; esac
161:      ;;
162:  esac
163:}

+verify_sha256() {
+  local file="$1" sum_url="$2" expected actual
+  if ! command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
