#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

Cache it per resolved version with `setup/cache.sh dart` (`DART_CACHE_*`).
Network-free inspection: `dart.sh plan` (resolved target/URL/layout) and
`dart.sh status`. Unit-tested in `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`.

Dart-repo runners wire it via `customParams.setupCommands`:
`["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]` (see `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` §3.3).

## Fixed — full version token + managed-install probing

**`setup/dart.sh`**

1. **Truncation (the reported bug)** — `installed_version` now captures the full banner token: `sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p'` — `3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …` → `3.14.0-315.1.beta`, so `have` equals what `channel_latest` resolves on **every** channel and the version-aware cache hit fires instead of wiping + re-downloading ~215 MB per leg.
2. **Foreign PATH dart (the related note)** — `installed_version` now probes the **managed install first** (`[ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]`), PATH second; and the cache-hit early-return additionally requires `[ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]`, so a matching foreign PATH dart can never take the hit branch and register a nonexistent `${SDK_BIN}` / point `DART_HOME` at nothing.
3. **Truncated `DART_VERSION` export** — `dart.sh` no longer re-exports `DART_VERSION` at all (see thread 2 — it is now a pure input pin), so no truncated value can reach `GITHUB_ENV`.

**Tests** (`js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`, all RED before the fix, GREEN after):

- `status parses the FULL token from a beta banner — 3.14.0-315.1.beta` (the exact stub from this thread)
- `status parses the FULL token from a dev banner (3.15.0-27.0.dev)`
- `a managed <install-dir> dart wins over a foreign PATH dart` (stub SDK at `<DART_INSTALL_DIR>/dart-sdk/bin/dart` vs stub PATH dart)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"

      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

arguments.content:
## Fixed — key now follows the resolution; round-trips by construction

Took a combination of the two suggested options:

1. **`setup/cache.sh` `_cache_dart`** now resolves the key the way `dart.sh` does — `version="$(bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/dart.sh" plan | sed -n 's/^requested=//p')"` (explicit `dart:<version>` argument still wins; falls back to `stable` only if the plan call cannot run). So a beta-pinned repo keys `dart-beta-<os>` and an `sdk:`-pinned repo keys `dart-<version>-<os>` — at **both** the restore (`cache.sh keys dart`, pre-install) and save (`cache.sh save dart`, post-install) steps.
2. **`setup/dart.sh` no longer re-exports `DART_VERSION`** (option 2's first half, which is what makes option 1 round-trip): with the old re-export, the save step's `plan` call saw `DART_VERSION=<installed>` and would still have flipped the key to `dart-<installed>-…` — never the key the restore step looked for. With `DART_VERSION` kept a pure input pin, the environment is identical for both steps, so the derived keys are identical in every case (no env → key follows quality.yml; user-pinned env → same pin visible to both). This also fixes a latent sticky-pin bug: a second bare `dart.sh` in the same job used to see the re-exported installed version and pin to it instead of re-resolving the channel.

Docs updated to match: the `DART_VERSION` row in `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` and the cache paragraph in `README.md` now state the key tracks the resolved target and that `DART_VERSION` is not re-exported.

**Tests** (`js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`, new suite `DART_CACHE_KEY follows the target dart.sh actually resolves`, RED before the fix):

- `keys dart` on a beta-pinned repo → `key=dart-beta-…` and no `dart-stable-` (RED pre-fix: `dart-stable-`)
- `keys dart` on an sdk-pinned repo → `key=dart-3.9.4-…`
- no detection source → `key=dart-stable-…` (unchanged default, kept honest)
- explicit `dart:3.5.0` argument wins over plan resolution
- restore/save derive identical keys for the same `DART_VERSION` environment

{"newText":"_cache_dart() {
  # Dart SDK (gh-918: factory legs on dart repos need the same gate toolchain
  # as CI — setup/dart.sh resolves the channel/version and installs under
  # ~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk). Key on the target dart.sh ACTUALLY resolves — the
  # same precedence (explicit dart:<version> arg > DART_VERSION env >
  # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart detection > stable) — so the key the
  # restore step computes ("cache.sh keys dart", BEFORE the install) is the
  # key the save step derives after it, and the primary key can round-trip.
  # (Keying on ${DART_VERSION:-stable} alone keyed the env var, not the
  # resolution: on a beta-pinned repo the restore step exported dart-stable-…
  # while dart.sh installed beta.) dart.sh keeps DART_VERSION a pure input
  # pin — it does not re-export the installed version under it — so this plan
  # call resolves identically before and after the install.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not

quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;

  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

Cache it per resolved version with `setup/cache.sh dart` (`DART_CACHE_*`).
Network-free inspection: `dart.sh plan` (resolved target/URL/layout) and
`dart.sh status`. Unit-tested in `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`.

Dart-repo runners wire it via `customParams.setupCommands`:
`["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]` (see `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` §3.3).

{"content":"## Fixed — key now follows the resolution; round-trips by construction

Took a combination of the two suggested options:

1. **`setup/cache.sh` `_cache_dart`** now resolves the key the way `dart.sh` does — `version="$(bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/dart.sh" plan | sed -n 's/^requested=//p')"` (explicit `dart:<version>` argument still wins; falls back to `stable` only if the plan call cannot run). So a beta-pinned repo keys `dart-beta-<os>` and an `sdk:`-pinned repo keys `dart-<version>-<os>` — at **both** the restore (`cache.sh keys dart`, pre-install) and save (`cache.sh save dart`, post-install) steps.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

Cache it per resolved version with `setup/cache.sh dart` (`DART_CACHE_*`).
Network-free inspection: `dart.sh plan` (resolved target/URL/layout) and
`dart.sh status`. Unit-tested in `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`.

Dart-repo runners wire it via `customParams.setupCommands`:
`["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]` (see `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` §3.3).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

Cache it per resolved version with `setup/cache.sh dart` (`DART_CACHE_*`).
Network-free inspection: `dart.sh plan` (resolved target/URL/layout) and
`dart.sh status`. Unit-tested in `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`.

Dart-repo runners wire it via `customParams.setupCommands`:
`["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]` (see `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` §3.3).

{"path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md","content":"## Fixed — full version token + managed-install probing

**`setup/dart.sh`**

1. **Truncation (the reported bug)** — `installed_version` now captures the full banner token: `sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p'` — `3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …` → `3.14.0-315.1.beta`, so `have` equals what `channel_latest` resolves on **every** channel and the version-aware cache hit fires instead of wiping + re-downloading ~215 MB per leg.

{"content":"## Fixed — key now follows the resolution; round-trips by construction

Took a combination of the two suggested options:

1. **`setup/cache.sh` `_cache_dart`** now resolves the key the way `dart.sh` does — `version="$(bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/dart.sh" plan | sed -n 's/^requested=//p')"` (explicit `dart:<version>` argument still wins; falls back to `stable` only if the plan call cannot run). So a beta-pinned repo keys `dart-beta-<os>` and an `sdk:`-pinned repo keys `dart-<version>-<os>` — at **both** the restore (`cache.sh keys dart`, pre-install) and save (`cache.sh save dart`, post-install) steps.
2. **`setup/dart.sh` no longer re-exports `DART_VERSION`** (option 2's first half, which is what makes option 1 round-trip): with the old re-export, the save step's `plan` call saw `DART_VERSION=<installed>` and would still have flipped the key to `dart-<installed>-…` — never the key the restore step looked for. With `DART_VERSION` kept a pure input pin, the environment is identical for both steps, so the derived keys are identical in every case (no env → key follows quality.yml; user-pinned env → same pin visible to both). This also fixes a latent sticky-pin bug: a second bare `dart.sh` in the same job used to see the re-exported installed version and pin to it instead of re-resolving the channel.

Docs updated to match: the `DART_VERSION` row in `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` and the cache paragraph in `README.md` now state the key tracks the resolved target and that `DART_VERSION` is not re-exported.

**Tests** (`js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`, new suite `DART_CACHE_KEY follows the target dart.sh actually resolves`, RED before the fix):

- `keys dart` on a beta-pinned repo → `key=dart-beta-…` and no `dart-stable-` (RED pre-fix: `dart-stable-`)
- `keys dart` on an sdk-pinned repo → `key=dart-3.9.4-…`
- no detection source → `key=dart-stable-…` (unchanged default, kept honest)
- explicit `dart:3.5.0` argument wins over plan resolution
- restore/save derive identical keys for the same `DART_VERSION` environment

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart
            # channel/sdk detection, else stable
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Precedence (sets TARGET/MODE/CHANNEL/VERSION/SOURCE):
#   1. explicit argument           → source=argument
#   2. DART_VERSION env            → source=environment
#   3. quality.yml sdk:/channel:   → source=quality workflow
#   4. stable                      → source=default
# A pinned version rides the DETECTED channel (setup-dart keeps using the
# channel for a full version), so leg output keeps matching CI exactly.
resolve_target() {
  local arg="${1:-}"
  TARGET="${arg:-${DART_VERSION:-}}"
  SOURCE="default"
  if [ -n "${arg}" ]; then
    SOURCE="argument"
  elif [ -n "${DART_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE="environment"
  fi

  local det found det_sdk det_channel
  det="$(quality_detection)"
  found="${det%%|*}"; det="${det#*|}"
  det_sdk="${det%%|*}"; det_channel="${det#*|}"

  if [ -z "${TARGET}" ]; then
    [ "${found}" = "1" ] && SOURCE="quality workflow"
    # A quality-workflow `sdk:` pin IS a target — the leg runs the exact
    # version CI runs; its `channel:` (or stable) then carries the download.
    [ -n "${det_sdk}" ] && TARGET="${det_sdk}"
  fi

  # Validate the target BEFORE it becomes a URL — a mistyped argument
  # ("--help", "instal") used to resolve as a version and die much later as a
  # bare curl 404 on .../release/--help/sdk/dartsdk-….zip, reading like a CDN
  # problem instead of a usage error.
  # A leading `v` is muscle memory from the v-prefixed pins of the sibling
  # installers (fa.sh v0.1.324 / dmtools.sh) — dart-archive URLs are
  # unprefixed, so strip it.
  TARGET="${TARGET#v}"
  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev) ;;
    [0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;;  # full version tokens: 3.9.4 / 3.14.0-315.1.beta
    *)
      echo "❌ unknown target '${TARGET}' (stable|beta|dev|latest|<version> like 3.9.4)" >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac

  case "${TARGET}" in
    ""|latest|stable|beta|dev)
      MODE="channel"
      CHANNEL="${TARGET}"
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ] || [ "${CHANNEL}" = "latest" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_channel}"; fi
      if [ -z "${CHANNEL}" ]; then CHANNEL="${det_sdk:+stable}"; fi

### Dart SDK (agent legs on Dart repos)

`setup/install.sh dart` (or `setup/dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]`,
env `DART_VERSION`) provisions the Dart SDK for machine-factory leg sessions —
the same gap the golden-test Flutter toolchain covers for fa legs (gh-918):
hosted runner images ship no `dart`, so a rework leg on a Dart repo could not
run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check` and claimed success while
quality-gate violations stayed in place. The installer:

- resolves the target exactly the way the repo's CI does — explicit
  argument/env first, then the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `sdk:`/`channel:`
  inputs in the checked-out repo's `.github/workflows/*.yml` ("same channel
  the repo's quality.yml uses"), else `stable`;
- downloads the SDK from the same dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart`
  uses, so leg-local gate output matches CI gate output;
- installs under `~/.dart-sdk/dart-sdk` (override `DART_INSTALL_DIR`), registers
  `bin` on PATH for the leg session (and subsequent CI steps), and exports
  `DART_HOME` / `DART_VERSION`;
- is version-aware: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on mismatch
  (pool VMs keep a persistent `$HOME` — a presence-only check lets an ancient
  binary shadow the requested toolchain forever).

Cache it per resolved version with `setup/cache.sh dart` (`DART_CACHE_*`).
Network-free inspection: `dart.sh plan` (resolved target/URL/layout) and
`dart.sh status`. Unit-tested in `js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js`.

Dart-repo runners wire it via `customParams.setupCommands`:
`["bash agents/setup/dart.sh"]` (see `docs/machine-factory-integration.md` §3.3).

{"content":"## Fixed — key now follows the resolution; round-trips by construction

Took a combination of the two suggested options:

1. **`setup/cache.sh` `_cache_dart`** now resolves the key the way `dart.sh` does — `version="$(bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/dart.sh" plan | sed -n 's/^requested=//p')"` (explicit `dart:<version>` argument still wins; falls back to `stable` only if the plan call cannot run). So a beta-pinned repo keys `dart-beta-<os>` and an `sdk:`-pinned repo keys `dart-<version>-<os>` — at **both** the restore (`cache.sh keys dart`, pre-install) and save (`cache.sh save dart`, post-install) steps.
2. **`setup/dart.sh` no longer re-exports `DART_VERSION`** (option 2's first half, which is what makes option 1 round-trip): with the old re-export, the save step's `plan` call saw `DART_VERSION=<installed>` and would still have flipped the key to `dart-<installed>-…` — never the key the restore step looked for. With `DART_VERSION` kept a pure input pin, the environment is identical for both steps, so the derived keys are identical in every case (no env → key follows quality.yml; user-pinned env → same pin visible to both). +# dart-archive publishes a .sha256 sidecar next to every SDK bundle. Verify
+# the downloaded zip against it — cheap supply-chain insurance for a ~215 MB
+# fetch that runs on every Dart-repo leg. A mismatch is fatal; a MISSING
+# sidecar (or no sha256 tool on PATH) only warns, so a CDN hiccup cannot red
+# the whole leg on an already-downloaded artifact.
+verify_sha256() {
+  local file="$1" sum_url="$2" expected actual
+  if ! command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "⚠️  no sha256sum/shasum on PATH — skipping SDK checksum verification" >&2
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if ! curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 "${sum_url}" -o "${file}.sha256"; then
+    echo "⚠️  sha256 sidecar unavailable (${sum_url}) — skipping checksum verification" >&2
+    return 0
+  fi
+  expected="$(cut -d' ' -f1 "${file}.sha256" | head -1)"
+  actual="$(hash_file "${file}")"
+  if [ -z "${expected}" ] || [ "${actual}" != "${expected}" ]; then
+    echo "❌ Dart SDK checksum mismatch (expected ${expected:-<none>}, got ${actual})" >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+  echo "🔐 Dart SDK checksum verified (${actual})"
+}
